design.approach: Fix the broken typed-question integration and key loading first, then register advisory review/judge points, add a redacted host-mediated consult seam, and wire advisory-first consumption in every skill with a review/judge/adversarial role, guarded by a deterministic boundary guard.
dataFlow: user opts in (existing --use-jev or request/2 decision block) -> driver builds adapter under existing env gate; key resolved via env var or repo .env
skill role -> consult seam builds one `questions` record for its advisory points -> transport -> provider descriptor
provider returns `answers` envelope -> seam maps per-question answers to points -> redacted evidence sidecar (untracked)
skill consumes advisory verdicts for routing/pre-flagging -> LLM/primary fallback on transport failure
deterministic guard + receipt + acceptance remain harness-owned and untouched; csm-orchestrate gate byte-identical
neverJev: the csm-orchestrate reviewAcceptance deterministic gate and final-review status
the csm-plan acceptance-signal lint (BL2) and applicability authority
the csm-autoresearch deterministic hard gates and csm-bdd-tdd primary VERIFY gate

acceptanceCriteria: AC1: Both shipped descriptors emit a typed `questions` record and parse the `answers` envelope, proven against raw-envelope fixtures.
AC2: The key resolver reads the descriptor env var or the repo .env, isolates providers, and never exposes a key on argv or in artifacts.
AC3: The new advisory points validate; no apply-classified point is safety/authority; decision-points.json stays in lockstep.
AC4: With the existing opt-in active the consult seam returns advisory verdicts and fails open on transport failure; without opt-in there is no adapter and no network.
AC5: Every listed skill consumes advisory verdicts for its review/judge/adversarial roles, including csm-build REVIEW, while all gates stay deterministic.
AC6: The boundary guard rejects advisory payloads in digest/receipt/gate/acceptance inputs; the orchestrate deterministic gate output is byte-identical with and without advice.
AC7: make test and make check are green and regenerated payload digests match.
constraints: Hook to the EXISTING opt-in (--use-jev / request-2 decision block); do not add a new Jev option or flag.
Preserve provider-pluggable suppliers: descriptor-only extension (OpenRouter default; Vercel supported but not live-verified now).

No gate authority: acceptance, security, completion, receipts, loop guards, closure, severity/evidence-class authority, and the csm-orchestrate deterministic reviewAcceptance gate stay deterministic and outside Jev.
Keys are resolved host-side only, never on argv and never in artifacts.
deliverables: Descriptor-level repair so shipped descriptors match the live typed-question API (questions record, answers envelope).
A provider key resolver that reads the descriptor's env var or falls back to the repo .env.
Safety/authority advisory decision points for every review/judge/adversarial role (including four separate judge-rubric Score points).
A host-mediated consult seam with the key loader, redaction, and fail-open, active only under the existing opt-in.
Advisory-first wiring in csm-review, csm-review-python, csm-deep-research, csm-plan, csm-build, csm-autoresearch, csm-bdd-tdd, and the bounded csm-orchestrate injected reviewer.
A deterministic never-Jev boundary guard, an advisory-agreement harness, docs, and regenerated payload.
exclusions: No implementation or execution in this planning run.
No live Vercel verification now (descriptor stays protocol-conformant and pluggable).
No wiring of Jev into the deterministic csm-orchestrate reviewAcceptance gate.
No new provider transport; the existing injected transport is reused.
No claim of measured per-role accuracy; no threshold promotion.
goal.summary: Fix the broken Jev provider integration first, then make every skill that performs review, judge, or adversarial-review judgment use the existing optional Jev layer as an advisory first pass for those roles (LLM retained for rationale/remediation and as fail-open fallback). Hook to the EXISTING opt-in only, keep provider-pluggable suppliers (Vercel deferred but supported), and let skills load the provider key from an env var or the repo .env when needed.
